title: Greek Avgolemono Soup
description: Chicken, carrots, rice and lemon, finished with eggs stirred in until the soup is thick and silky. Four portions for two nights, with Parmesan if we’re feeling cheesy.
difficulty: Take your time with the eggs
portionNote: The soup base makes 4 portions for two dinners for both of us. The eggs and pepper listed in each choice are for that night’s two-portion dinner.
imageAlt: Silky Greek avgolemono soup with chicken, carrots, rice and lemon in a white bowl.
personalNote: Don’t worry if the broth tastes a bit flat before the lemon and eggs. Keep the salt a little low, especially if we’re having Parmesan. We can always add a bit at the table, but we can’t take it out.
equipment: Very large pot with a lid
advancePrep: Chop the chicken and vegetables and boil the kettle. For the second dinner, pick the saved-base tab so we start with the refrigerated soup instead of cooking the whole recipe again. The onions, garlic and other veg don’t have to be chopped really fine or look uniform. They’ll soften and cook down while the soup bubbles, so don’t spend ages making everything match.
importantNotes: Keep the soup quite runny before adding the eggs. Whisk a little hot broth into the beaten eggs first, then pour them back in slowly while stirring vigorously over very low heat. Once the eggs go in, keep it below a boil.
choiceHeading: Making the batch, or having the second dinner?
choiceIntro: The first choice makes the soup base for both nights and finishes tonight’s dinner. The second starts with the saved soup and finishes it with 2 eggs.

recipeOptions.label: Make the batch
recipeOptions.description: Cook the soup base for both nights, put tomorrow’s soup aside, then finish tonight’s dinner with 2 eggs and the measured pepper.

groups.title: For the soup base — both nights

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.note: Or use 6 small carrots for the full batch. Dice.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.note: Boil before starting. Add more boiling water later if needed to keep the soup runny.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: Only a tiny bit if very undersalted; have some at the table if serving without Parmesan.

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.note: To serve, if we’re feeling cheesy.

afterSteps.title: Chop everything and boil the kettle
afterSteps.description: Chop the chicken. Dice the onions and carrots and roughly chop the head of garlic. Boil a kettle of water.
afterSteps.tip: The onions, garlic and other veg don’t have to be chopped really fine or look uniform. They’ll soften and cook down while the soup bubbles, so don’t spend ages making everything match.

afterSteps.title: Start the chicken and vegetables together
afterSteps.description: Heat a large pot on medium heat. Add the chicken, onions, garlic and carrots and fry for 10 minutes, moving everything around, until the chicken is white on the outside and the vegetables have started softening.

afterSteps.title: Add the herbs, stock and water
afterSteps.description: Add the mixed herbs or dried thyme, whichever we have, the chicken stock cubes and the bay leaves. Pour in the kettle of boiled water and mix it around.

afterSteps.title: Put the lid on and let it bubble
afterSteps.description: Bring the soup to a gentle bubble, cover and cook on low heat for 30 minutes. Wash and drain the rice while it cooks.

afterSteps.title: Taste lightly, take out the bay leaves and add lemon
afterSteps.description: Open the pot and check the chicken is cooked through before tasting the broth. If it is very undersalted, add a tiny bit of salt. If it feels alright, leave it alone. It’s meant to taste a bit flat for now. Fish out the bay leaves and throw them away, then add the lemon juice.
afterSteps.tip: We’re keeping the salt a little low because Parmesan adds more at the table.

afterSteps.title: Add the washed rice
afterSteps.description: Add the washed, drained rice, cover again and let it cook at a gentle boil for 20 minutes. Check the rice is tender before moving on.

afterSteps.title: Keep it quite runny
afterSteps.description: Open the pot and check the water level. The soup should still be quite runny. If it has thickened too much, add more boiling water and stir until it loosens up. The eggs will thicken it again.

afterSteps.title: Put tomorrow’s soup aside
afterSteps.description: Put tomorrow’s half of the soup base aside to cool quickly and refrigerate. Keep tonight’s soup in the pot, ready for the egg finish.
afterSteps.tip: The second-night tab starts with this saved base. Because it contains rice, use the refrigerated portion within 24 hours, or freeze it for later.

afterSteps.title: Beat 2 eggs
afterSteps.description: Beat 2 eggs in a heatproof bowl and keep them ready for the next step.

afterSteps.title: Warm the eggs with a little hot broth
afterSteps.description: Turn the heat right down so the soup is no longer bubbling. Whisk a little hot liquid from the soup into the beaten eggs, starting with a small trickle. Add a little more gradually while whisking constantly, until the eggs feel warm. This helps them mix smoothly into the soup.
afterSteps.tip: We’re using broth from the pot, so there’s no extra water or extra lemon to add here.

afterSteps.title: Stir it into something silky
afterSteps.description: Slowly pour the warmed egg mixture into the soup while stirring vigorously, like we do for carbonara. Keep stirring on very low heat for about 5 minutes, until it becomes thick and silky. Keep it below a boil so the eggs don’t scramble.
afterSteps.doneness: Thick and silky, with no scrambled pieces. Heat the finished soup to at least 75°C, keeping it below a boil.

afterSteps.title: Pepper, then serve
afterSteps.description: Add the pepper powder, mix one last time and serve. Add Parmesan if we’re feeling cheesy, but it’s lovely on its own too. Have some salt on the side if we’re skipping the Parmesan.
afterSteps.tip: Parmesan has salt in it, so we’ve kept the soup a little less salty. Better to add a little at the table than have too much in the pot.

recipeOptions.label: Second dinner · saved base
recipeOptions.description: Reheat the saved soup, loosen it with boiling water and finish it with 2 eggs and the measured pepper. This is two portions for tonight.

ingredients.name: Saved chicken, rice and lemon soup base
ingredients.note: The half saved before adding eggs and pepper; for the second dinner for both of us.

ingredients.name: Extra boiling water
ingredients.note: As needed to loosen the saved soup.

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.note: To serve, if we’re feeling cheesy.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: At the table if serving without Parmesan.

afterSteps.title: Reheat the saved base and loosen it
afterSteps.description: Put the saved half of the soup base into a pot and reheat until it is steaming hot all the way through, stirring so it heats evenly. The rice will have absorbed more liquid in the fridge, so add boiling water until it is quite runny again. Then turn the heat right down before adding the eggs.
ingredients: Saved chicken, rice and lemon soup base
afterSteps.tip: Use the refrigerated rice soup within 24 hours, or thaw a safely frozen portion in the fridge before reheating.
afterSteps.doneness: Base steaming hot throughout before the fresh egg finish.

afterSteps.title: Beat 2 eggs
afterSteps.description: Beat 2 eggs in a heatproof bowl and keep them ready for the next step.

afterSteps.title: Warm the eggs with a little hot broth
afterSteps.description: Turn the heat right down so the soup is no longer bubbling. Whisk a little hot liquid from the soup into the beaten eggs, starting with a small trickle. Add a little more gradually while whisking constantly, until the eggs feel warm. This helps them mix smoothly into the soup.
afterSteps.tip: We’re using broth from the pot, so there’s no extra water or extra lemon to add here.

afterSteps.title: Stir it into something silky
afterSteps.description: Slowly pour the warmed egg mixture into the soup while stirring vigorously, like we do for carbonara. Keep stirring on very low heat for about 5 minutes, until it becomes thick and silky. Keep it below a boil so the eggs don’t scramble.

afterSteps.title: Finish with pepper and serve
afterSteps.description: Add the pepper powder and mix one last time. Serve with Parmesan if we fancy it, or leave it plain and have some salt on the side.

substitutions.title: Whichever dried herbs we have
substitutions.text: Use 1 tablespoon mixed herbs or dried thyme for the full batch.

substitutions.title: Large or small carrots
substitutions.text: Use 4 large carrots or 6 small ones for the full batch.

substitutions.title: Parmesan or no Parmesan
substitutions.text: It’s lovely on its own. If we skip the Parmesan, keep some salt on the side so we can add a little at the table.

troubleshooting.title: It has become too thick
troubleshooting.text: Add more boiling water before the eggs so the soup is quite runny. The rice also absorbs liquid in the fridge, so loosen the saved base when reheating.

troubleshooting.title: Keeping the eggs silky
troubleshooting.text: Warm the beaten eggs gradually with a little hot broth while whisking, then pour them back into the pot slowly while stirring vigorously. Keep the heat very low and do not let it boil.

troubleshooting.title: It tastes a little flat early on
troubleshooting.text: That’s alright. Add only a tiny bit of salt if it is very undersalted. The lemon, eggs, pepper and optional Parmesan still have to go in.

storage: Cool the saved base quickly in shallow containers, refrigerate promptly and use within 24 hours because it contains rice. Freeze it if the second dinner will be later.
reheating: Reheat the saved base once until steaming hot throughout, adding boiling water to loosen it. Then use the second-night tab to temper and stir in 2 beaten eggs over very low heat, finishing with the measured pepper.
foodSafety: Cook the chicken fully before tasting the broth. Check the chicken and finished soup with a clean food thermometer: at least 75°C. Keep the egg finish below a boil.
servingSuggestion: Four portions across two nights. Serve with Parmesan if we’re feeling cheesy, or enjoy it plain with a little salt on the side.
